title: Where does the lift reach after plus four and minus four?
description: The lift starts on the ground floor, goes up four floors and then comes down four floors. The two presses are added to find where the lift reaches. Keeko thinks the lift reaches floor eight because four and four make eight, and the second press going down breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: a press and its inverse bring the lift back to the start, so the sum is zero. Watch for students who add the numbers without the signs.

source: If Basant now presses +4 and then presses −4 in the lift, wh
video_script.why: A child sees that a press followed by its inverse leaves the lift where it began, which is the idea behind a sum of zero.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lift on the ground floor, with plus four followed by minus four
video_script.anchor: Ziva in the lift of Ruhee, starting on the ground floor, pressing plus four and then minus four
video_script.wrong_move: adds the two counts four and four and ignores that the second press goes down
video_script.payoff_line: Going up some floors and then down the same floors ends at the start.

final_answer.spoken: floor zero, which is the ground floor

names.Ziva: pressed plus three by mistake on the ground floor and cancelled it with minus three
names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: the target floor before the answer
maths_rules: +4 takes the lift from the ground floor up four floors.
−4 takes it down the same four floors.
video_script.design: One idea: a press and its inverse bring the lift back to the start. One lift picture throughout; the two arrows are drawn on one line. Keeko's doubt is broken by the second arrow pointing down.
